metadataRevisions.removed: Strategic choice exists in a narrow temporal zone: fast enough that decisions can be revisited, slow enough that evidence can accumulate. Collapse it from either direction and strategy disappears.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Strategy needs time: enough to revisit a decision, and enough for its consequences to become visible.

metadataRevisions.removed: On the strange process of extracting what you know but cannot say, and why it requires watching more than asking.

metadataRevisions.removed: On discovering that machines can be peers, and on the division of cognitive labor that makes partnership possible.

metadataRevisions.removed: On discovering that a single perspective—even a smart one—is never enough to see what you're actually thinking.
metadataRevisions.replacement: On using a staged critic to expose an objection, and why simulated perspectives do not replace colleagues.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for note:why-you-need-multiple-minds.

metadataRevisions.removed: Peter Kingsley reveals that Western philosophy originated through deliberate transmission of Central Asian shamanic wisdom to ancient Greece.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Peter Kingsley argues that Western philosophy carried an initiatory inheritance that its later rational self-description obscured.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:a-story-waiting-to-pierce-you.

metadataRevisions.removed: James Nestor on how modern humans breathe wrong, and what ancient traditions knew about it.
metadataRevisions.replacement: James Nestor’s popular account of slower nasal breathing, and the limits of treating it as clinical guidance.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:breath.

metadataRevisions.removed: Nestor explains how nasal and slower breathing affect nervous-system regulation.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Nestor assembles historical practices and physiological studies on slower nasal breathing; this annotation treats the book as inquiry, not clinical guidance.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:breath.

metadataRevisions.removed: A student saying "I'm not religious, but I'm not not-religious either." Kronman maps the philosophical territory that gap occupies.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Kronman maps the territory between institutional faith and a wholly disenchanted account of the world.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:confessions-of-a-born-again-pagan.

metadataRevisions.removed: Watching a boardroom where both sides claimed victory yet both lost something essential. The distinction named what was happening.
metadataRevisions.replacement: A contract can settle terms and still damage the relationship needed to carry them. Carse gives that tension a name.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:finite-and-infinite-games.

metadataRevisions.removed: Elinor Ostrom's Nobel Prize-winning work demonstrates that communities can manage shared resources without external control—and offers design principles for institutions that work.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Elinor Ostrom’s cases of communities managing shared resources, and the design questions those cases make inspectable.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:governing-the-commons.

metadataRevisions.removed: Eric D. Schneider and Dorion Sagan on how the second law of thermodynamics drives life, complexity, and evolution.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Eric D. Schneider and Dorion Sagan’s thermodynamic account of biological complexity.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:into-the-cool.

metadataRevisions.removed: Viktor Frankl's profound insight: meaning can be found even in the most brutal circumstances, and this search for meaning is our primary human drive.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Viktor Frankl’s account of meaning under suffering and the therapeutic propositions he later developed as logotherapy.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:mans-search-for-meaning.

metadataRevisions.removed: A student asked what to do when the work stops meaning anything. Frankl wrote from the one place where that question couldn't be avoided.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Frankl asks how meaning can remain available under suffering without claiming that meaning explains who survives.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:mans-search-for-meaning.

metadataRevisions.removed: Neil Theise shows how complexity theory reveals the universe as a seamless, self-organizing whole—and why consciousness might be fundamental.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Neil Theise on self-organization, emergence, and his separate argument that consciousness may be fundamental.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:notes-on-complexity.

metadataRevisions.removed: Philip Shepherd on why Western culture systematically trained us to live in our heads, and what pelvic intelligence can teach us about being whole.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Philip Shepherd’s argument that Western culture privileges head-centered attention, and his practice of pelvic intelligence.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:radical-wholeness.

metadataRevisions.removed: A moment in yoga when a student stops thinking about the body and starts thinking from it. Shepherd explains why that distinction is a Copernican revolution.
metadataRevisions.replacement: In tree pose, balance can shift from conscious correction to embodied adjustment. Shepherd treats that shift as a challenge to the head’s rule.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:radical-wholeness.

metadataRevisions.removed: A beautifully designed restructuring that looked perfect on the whiteboard and fell apart within months. Scott explains why legibility projects destroy the knowledge they can't see.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Scott asks what a clean administrative map erases: local knowledge, informal coordination, and adaptation.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:seeing-like-a-state.

metadataRevisions.removed: Watching platform companies label worker protections as "friction to be optimized away." Polanyi saw this pattern a century ago.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Polanyi’s history asks what returns as “friction” when labor is treated as a commodity.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-great-transformation.

metadataRevisions.removed: A room full of executives falling silent. The silence where something becomes audible that was always there.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Mathieu asks what becomes audible when visual attention loosens its grip.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-listening-book.

metadataRevisions.removed: A review where every number was green. The project was dying. McGilchrist explains why this keeps happening.
metadataRevisions.replacement: A dashboard can stay green while the work underneath it fails. McGilchrist offers one account of what formal attention leaves out.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-matter-with-things.

metadataRevisions.removed: Reading the Iliad carefully, something is missing. The characters don't deliberate. Jaynes took that observation seriously and built a theory from it.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Jaynes reads the Iliad as containing little reflective deliberation and builds a theory of consciousness from that contested observation.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-origin-of-consciousness.

metadataRevisions.removed: Kahlil Gibran's timeless wisdom on love, work, freedom, and the integration of opposites.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Kahlil Gibran’s prose poems on love, work, freedom, and holding apparent opposites together.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:the-prophet.

metadataRevisions.removed: Someone giving this book at twenty. Understanding it at forty. The images didn't change; the capacity to receive them did.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Images that once felt merely beautiful now name tensions I recognize: intimacy without fusion, work without guaranteed outcomes.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-prophet.

metadataRevisions.removed: Tara Springett maps nine stages of consciousness development from unawareness to enlightenment, showing why different people need different kinds of help.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Tara Springett’s developmental map, and the caution required before applying stage models to other people.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:the-stairway-to-heaven.

metadataRevisions.removed: Two students tried the same meditation technique. One had a breakthrough. The other had a breakdown. Springett's developmental framework explains why.
metadataRevisions.replacement: A developmental map can make different responses to practice easier to discuss. It can also become a hierarchy mistaken for diagnosis.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:the-stairway-to-heaven.

metadataRevisions.removed: An organization that doubled its quality controls and watched defect rates go up. The intervention caused the problem. Meadows explains why.
metadataRevisions.replacement: An organization added quality gates and defect rates rose. Meadows offers a way to investigate the sequence without pretending it settles the cause.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:thinking-in-systems.

metadataRevisions.removed: Adrian Daub on Silicon Valley's recycled philosophy dressed in hoodies.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Adrian Daub on the older intellectual histories behind Silicon Valley’s claims of novelty.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:what-tech-calls-thinking.

metadataRevisions.removed: Stanley and Lehman's computational proof that objectives block discovery, validated through AI experiments.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Stanley and Lehman on novelty search, and the limits of extending its experimental results into a general theory of discovery.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public description claim for annotation:why-greatness-cannot-be-planned.

metadataRevisions.removed: The best product feature ever shipped wasn't on any roadmap. Stanley and Lehman proved computationally why this keeps happening.
metadataRevisions.replacement: Novelty search outperformed objective-driven search in particular experiments. What follows beyond those domains remains an open question.
metadataRevisions.reason: U7 bounds the public teaser claim for annotation:why-greatness-cannot-be-planned.
